s1.syndrome_frame: Acute spinal cord syndrome with rapid progression of neurological deficits following a surgical procedure
salient_findings: Development of hypesthesia below chest level
Reduction in muscle strength of both lower limbs progressing to flaccid paralysis
Space-occupying lesion at left epidural site with spinal compression
key_facts: No history of gestational diabetes mellitus, preeclampsia, or coagulation disorders
Emergency cesarean section due to amniotic fluid turbidity
Initial recovery of sensation and muscle strength in right lower limb
Mild soreness and swelling with MMT grade of 2 in left lower limb
MRI findings of space-occupying lesion at left epidural site

shortlist.label: Epidural hematoma
shortlist.why_kept: Emergency cesarean section with intraoperative blood loss and subsequent spinal compression

shortlist.label: Vascular malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Confirmed presence of vascular malformation on pathological examination and MRI findings of space-occupying lesion

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of neurological deficits following a surgical procedure and presence of space-occupying lesion

shortlist.label: Spinal cord infarction
shortlist.why_kept: Rapid progression of neurological deficits and presence of spinal compression

shortlist.label: Arteriovenous malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of vascular malformation and spinal compression with rapid progression of neurological deficits

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of hypesthesia below chest level, reduction in muscle strength of both lower limbs, and progression to flaccid paralysis after a cesarean section, combined with MRI findings of a space-occupying lesion at the left epidural site causing spinal compression, are most consistent with an epidural hematoma.

rejected.label: Vascular malformation
rejected.why: While the pathological examination confirmed the presence of a vascular malformation, the acute onset of neurological symptoms and the specific MRI findings are more indicative of an epidural hematoma.

rejected.label: Spinal epidural abscess
rejected.why: There is no mention of infection or abscess in the provided information, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Spinal cord infarction
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings do not specifically suggest a spinal cord infarction, and there is no clear indication of a vascular event leading to infarction.

rejected.label: Arteriovenous malformation
rejected.why: Although an arteriovenous malformation could explain some of the patient's symptoms, the MRI findings and the acute presentation are more consistent with an epidural hematoma.

gold: Spontaneous spinal epidural hematoma (SSEH) with underlying vascular malformation
